findings.title: The lifetime cliff
findings.body: At Lifetime L2 and L3, Vector succeeded 0/10 and 0/10, while Mem0 and Letta each completed 10/10 and 10/10. All four L2/L3 paired comparisons reject after Holm correction — the only statistically significant separations in the study.

findings.title: Vector owns the noise wall
findings.body: Vector kept perfect target retrieval and success in delayed recall (10/10) and every noise level (10/10, 10/10, 10/10). Mem0's Failure Point appeared at noise 30, Letta's at noise 50.

findings.title: Retrieval ≠ Behavior
findings.body: Across 320 runs: retrieval present + success 180, present + failure 22, absent + success 0, absent + failure 118. World update is the proof: every active backend retrieved the current fact in 10/10 runs, yet 17 of 30 still acted on stale memory. A retrieval-only benchmark would miss all 22.

findings.title: Absence is fatal
findings.body: NoMemory went 0/10 in every cell, and across all backends not a single run succeeded without retrieving the causal fact. Memory is necessary — and, as 22 runs show, not sufficient.
